svg.title: component decomposition used by CE3. Each Cg depends only on the test germ at x −πgx by CE2; singleton normals are zero. For partitions Q, R both separated on a test support, Q i∈Q Si expands into corrections indexed by partitions refining Q, since choices of partitions inside its parts are exactly such refinements. A term not refining R has a group crossing two R parts. At its collapse those labels coincide, whereas they remain separated on the test support. Its germ- dependent factor annihilates the test, which is zero near that collapsed locus. All such crossing terms vanish as scores after multiplication by the test mask. Both expansions therefore reduce to common refinements, as masked scores before evaluation and integration. This proves the overlap identity even for nonnested Q, R used in CE15.
